conceptZh: 一棵頑皮的木頭玩具樹被松果頂到，驚訝地打直身軀並張開雙手雙腳，形成標準的「木」字。
object: a comical carved-wood toy tree with a central trunk, upper cross-branch, and springy root legs
morph: The top branches snap into a straight horizontal stroke, the trunk forms a sturdy vertical line, and the root legs pop outward into symmetrical left and right diagonal strokes.
creativeAngle: 專為低年級男童設計的肢體喜劇效果：利用松果掉落誘發玩具樹伸展出大字型搞笑姿勢，將樹枝與樹根精準對應至「木」字的一橫、一豎、一撇、一捺，兼具趣味性與正確字形結構。
promptEn:
An 8-second 3D animated educational video for Taiwanese children teaching the Traditional Chinese character '木' (mù, tree).

[0:00-0:02] Staging: Against a soft, bright cream background, a cute chunky wooden toy tree stands centered. A comical acorn drops onto its head with a playful squeak.

[0:02-0:05] Slapstick Morph: Startled, the toy tree hilariously freezes into a rigid gymnastic pose. Its top branch snaps flat into a solid horizontal stroke (一), its trunk straightens into a vertical line (丨), and its root legs pop outward into a left diagonal stroke (丿) and right diagonal stroke (乀). The object transforms cleanly into the dark, solid-colored Traditional Chinese character '木', centered and occupying about 70% of the frame height.

[0:05-0:08] Static Hold & Audio: The scene holds completely still for a full 3 seconds on the legible, high-contrast glyph '木'. Clear Taiwanese Mandarin voiceover pronounces 'ㄇㄨˋ' (mù) four times: 'ㄇㄨˋ... ㄇㄨˋ... ㄇㄨˋ... ㄇㄨˋ!'. Pure composition with no extra text, clutter, or visual noise.
direction: 帶一點小男孩會喜歡的搞笑

conceptZh: 太空人玩偶想敲敲木頭做的「木」，輕輕一敲卻把自己彈得翻了一圈；抱穩筆畫後，終於敲出清脆的木頭聲。
object: A single freestanding wooden 木 sculpture and an original bouncy astronaut toy with a fishbowl helmet.
morph: Begin with the complete, correctly formed glyph. Its four wooden strokes remain rigid and unchanged as the astronaut's knocking reveals the material.
creativeAngle: 不再讓玩具樹受驚變字，改用完整木字當木頭道具。自信滿滿的太空人一敲就失重翻圈，再抱穩筆畫輕敲成功；笑點來自玩偶的反作用力，字形始終正確。
promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second stylized 3D animation featuring one original astronaut toy with stubby molded limbs, a bright orange suit, and an oversized transparent fishbowl helmet. It is proudly determined but keeps drifting off the ground at inconvenient moments. Its only companion object is a freestanding wooden Traditional Chinese glyph 木.

Use a locked frontal camera and a light warm cream studio background. From the opening frame, center the complete 木, uncropped, at approximately 70% of frame height with generous margins. Build it as one rigid, shallow wooden sculpture with saturated solid burnt-sienna front faces: one horizontal stroke, one central vertical extending above and below the horizontal, and distinct left-falling and right-falling strokes spreading from the central junction. Preserve a standard, readable printed character silhouette throughout. Subtle side bevels suggest wood without adding marks across the stroke faces.

At 0.0–1.3 seconds, the small astronaut floats up beside the right end of the horizontal stroke, puffs out its chest, and winds up one tiny fist to knock. Pause briefly in proud anticipation. At 1.3–3.0 seconds, its tiny knock makes a gentle hollow wooden tok. The heavy 木 stays perfectly still, but the astronaut slowly tumbles backward through one complete somersault in the open space beside it, boots passing over its helmet. Its confident expression becomes wide-eyed surprise; keep the whole tumble visible within the frame.

At 3.0–4.4 seconds, it returns, braces both arms around the outer tip of the right-falling stroke, and gives a much smaller fingertip tap. A soft wooden tick: this time it stays put. It beams, releases its grip, and drifts into a seated pose in the lower-right margin, clear of every stroke.

From 4.4–8.0 seconds, hold the finished 木 completely still and unobstructed, with the astronaut resting quietly beside it. A warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin, exactly: 「木、木、木頭」. Time the first 木 near 0.4 seconds, the second near 3.1 seconds, and 木頭 near 5.5 seconds, with comfortable pauses. Stop after the word. Keep sound effects soft and use no music. Only 木 appears as on-screen writing; no vocabulary labels, subtitles, other text, logos, watermarks, clutter, or flashing effects.
